art.subject: Cotton Pygmy Goose (Nettapus coromandelianus), adult male in breeding plumage, as on a lowland pond in early summer: forehead and crown blackish; face, head and neck white; a black, green-glossed collar around the base of the neck; back, scapulars and wings dark glossy green; breast and underparts white, the flanks finely vermiculated pale grey; tail blackish. Bill very short, stubby and black; legs and feet dark grey.
art.pose: swimming among floating water-lily leaves, side view
art.scene: small lowland pond in southern Korea in early summer, covered with floating leaves; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding, side view swimming: tiny compact duck, small rounded head with a black crown, white face and neck, blackish-green collar at the base of the neck, very short deep-based black bill, dark green-glossed back and wings, white breast, pale grey vermiculated flanks, short dark tail
adult female, side view swimming: dark crown, pale face and neck with a dark line through the eye, no collar, mottled breast, dull dark brown back and wings, very short dark bill

adult male, in flight seen squarely from above: head, body and tail in one line, wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, dark green-glossed wings crossed by a broad white band across the flight feathers, white head with a black crown, black collar
art.build: Tiny duck, one of the smallest waterfowl, clearly smaller than a Eurasian Teal; compact, with a small rounded head and short neck. Bill very short, much shorter than the head, deep at the base and goose-like. Legs short. In flight the male shows dark green wings crossed by a broad white band across the primaries and a white trailing edge to the secondaries; the female shows only the white trailing edge. Tail short, rounded and dark.
avoid: Do not paint it teal-sized or larger, or with a long, flat duck bill; it is tiny with a short goose-like bill.
Do not leave out the black breast collar of the breeding male.
Do not paint a dark or green head; the head is white with only a dark cap.
Do not paint chestnut or rufous flanks; the flanks are pale grey and white.
